University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees Committees Approved at Board Meeting on 6/26/2020 Amended 10/24/2020 University Advancement and External Affairs Committee Membership: At least three voting members of the Board are appointed annually by the Board Chair upon the recommendations of the Governance Committee and in consultation with the University president. The Board Chair will appoint a Chair and Vice Chair for the Committee. Purposes: The committee provides oversight of University initiatives, programs and resources intended to enhance public understanding and appreciation of the University and to foster positive engagement from local to the global arena. The committee is responsible for oversight of the University’s Academic Strategic Plan. This committee supports the University’s efforts to advance its reputation for the quality and distinctiveness of its programs, liaise with the URI Foundation to amplify the Uni versity’s fundraising efforts and stay informed of the University’s advocacy efforts before governmental and other public bodies. The Committee provides oversight of the goals, plans and strategies of the University’s marketing and communications program for internal and external audiences. The Committee periodically assesses and reports to the Board on the University’s standing and relationship with its public audiences, including academia, government and the global community. The Committee serves as a s ounding board on University public relations and marketing activities and initiatives.

The Committee partners with the URI Foundation and Alumni Engagement on advancing URI through fundraising. The Committee will receive periodic updates on progress towards fundraising and campaign goals. The Committee will review and assist the University on government relations efforts especially related to state financial support. University Liaisons: Executive Director, External Relations and Communications President, University of Rhode Island Foundation and Alumni Engagement

Institutional Risk and Compliance Committee Membership: At least three voting members of the Board are appointed annually by the Board Chair upon the recommendation of the Governance Committee and in consultation with the University President. The Board Chair will appoint a Chair and Vice Chair for the Committee. Purposes: The Committee assists the Board in maintaining the integrity of the University’s financial systems and in the effective management of risk, including that arising from noncompliance with laws and regulations, oversight of potential misbehaviors, and complex decisions with uncertain outcomes. The Committee will make recommendations to the Board in furtherance of their fiduciary obligations to minimize risk and preserve the reputation of the University. Due to its importance and impact on the University’s reputation, the Committee focuses on compliance with legal and professional standards governing the conduct of research and University responses to incidents that may compromise the integrity of the mission. The core functions of the Committee include: Oversight of internal audit plans and operations, including the University’s actions to correct identified weaknesses in internal controls;

Review of University financial statements, the conduct, conclusions and recommendations of external audits and approval of the University’s responses to management letters; Regular assessment of the effectiveness, security, and potential vulnerabilities of the University’s information technology and the information systems it supports. Review of prioritized institutional risk assessment and mitigation plans prepared by University management on existing or potential threats to the ability of the University to carry out its mission or achieve goals of the strategic plan. University Liaison: University General Counsel Vice President, Research & Economic Development Vice President for Administration and Finance

Finance and Facilities Committee Membership: At least three voting members of the Board are appointed annually by the Board Chair upon the recommendation of the Governance Committee and in consultation with the University President. The Board Chair will appoint a Chair and a Vice Chair for the committee. Purposes: A primary purpose of the committee is to oversee fulfillment of the Board’s fiduciary responsibility through the provision of appropriate human, physical, financial, and technology resources. The committee is responsible for the provision of the necessary physical and technological infrastructure to support the mission and strategic vision of the University. The committee reviews and recommends for Board approval, major capital projects, real estate transactions, material grounds development, and the development and implementation of the IT Strategic Plan. The committee reviews plans and requests for borrowing and submits them to the Board for approval. Specific duties include: Monitor the University’s financial operations; Review and recommend annual and long-range operating and capital budgets; Oversee that accurate and complete financial records are maintained; Review of the University financial statements and budgets and provide committee recommendations for Board approval; Facilitate the advancement of contemporary human resources systems, including progress in measuring and evaluation of community diversity and inclusion. Monitor campus facilities, grounds, maintenance, depreciation,

deferred maintenance, and asset protection investments; Oversee contemporary, efficient, and timely procurement processes and investments, especially for the continuous improvement of the information technology infrastructure; and Review that the long-range master plan for facilities is updated periodically. University Liaisons: Vice President for Administration and Finance, Chief Information Officer, Assistant Vice President, Human Resources

APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE UNIVERSITY TO BORROW MONEY IN THE NAME AND ON BEHALF OF THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES FOR EMERGENCY CONDITIONS DURING FISCAL YEAR 2021.
The University seeks approval of a resolution authorizing it to borrow money in the name and on behalf of the Board of Trustees for emergency conditions during FY 21.
The need for this authorization is driven by the delay in the state budget process, the uncertainty around how the second semester will unfold and the fact that the Board meets infrequently.
The borrowing authority will be for FY21 only and the amount borrowed will not exceed $10 million dollars.
It will also be subject to approval of the l egislature, the limitations of issuances of debt in our bond indentures , and other applicable laws and regulations.
The University President and Vice President of Administration and Finance, in consultation with the Board chair, must determine in writing the emergency conditions dictating the need to borrow.

The University President and/or Vice President for Administration and Finance shall report to the Board any borrowing of money made pursuant to this resolution which shall include the amount borrowed, the reason for the loan and a summary of the terms and conditions under which the money was borrowed, at its next regularly scheduled meeting or within thirty (30) days of the loan closing whichever shall first occur.
It is therefore recommended that the URI Board of Trustees approve the following resolution: RESOLVED THAT: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees (the “Board”) do es hereby authorize the University of Rhode Island to borrow money in the name and on behalf of the Board for emergen cy conditions during Fiscal Year 2021 subject to approval of the General Assembly, the limitation on issuance of debt in university bond indentures and other applicable laws and regulations.

The following additional conditions shall apply to the exercise of this authority: • This authority is limited to and shall not extend beyond Fiscal Year 2021 and the amount borrowed pursuant to this authority shall not exceed $10 million dollars. • The University President and Vice President for Administration and Financ e must first, in consultation with the Board chair, have determined and documented in writing, the emergency conditions dictating the need to borrow money pursuant to this authority.
All loan instruments and documents required to be signed by the lender in connection with the borrowing of money made pursuant to this authority shall require the signature of the Board chair and either the University President or Vice President for Administration and Finance.

The University President and/or Vice President for Administration and Finance shall report to the Board any borrowing of money made pursuant to this resolution which shall include the amount borrowed, the reason for the loan and a su mmary of the terms and conditions under which the money was borrowed, at its next regularly scheduled meeting or within thirty (30) days of the loan closing whichever shall first occur.

The financial statements and the budget are presented differently • The financial statements follow Government Accounting Standards Board (GASB) accounting rules, which incorporate accrual accounting principles • Include depreciation • Match revenues and expenses • Show interest but not the current principal portion of long term debt as an expense • Classify capital maintenance expenses as increases to capital assets, not an expense • Include the URI Foundation and Alumni Engagement and the URI Research Foundation as “component units” • Include estimates of State ERS pension and OPEB liabilities that are actuarially adjusted each year and allocated to the agencies • Reflect many eliminating entries for transfers between funds (e.g. Foundation to the University)

The financial statements and the budget are presented differently •The budget is based on cash accounting and divides the budget into Education & General (“unrestricted”) funds and Auxiliary, Sponsored Research and other (“restricted”) funds • Shows debt service on GO Bonds as “revenue” from the state, then shows a matching entry as an expense; the debt service is the obligation of the State • Revenues include the annual appropriation for the State Crime Lab • Federal loans and external scholarships included as revenue and expense - GASB treats as a pass-through • Operating expenses include maintenance items that are considered capital expenditures under GASB • Principal portion of debt service included as an expense • Auxiliary enterprises budget expenses to match anticipated revenue

Financial statements are important to the financial markets URI has two main types of debt obligations: •Revenue bonds – issued through RIHEBC and secured by a pledge of our Education and General (E&G) revenues or our Auxiliary (Aux) revenues - $292 mm •Certificates of Participation (COPS) – issued by the State, serviced by payments made by agencies (such as URI) to the State - $22 mm General Obligation (GO) bonds are obligations of the State of Rhode Island, not the University, and the State pays the debt service on them

The agencies that rate our bonds analyze our financial statements •GASB standardization permits comparisons among many financial institutions •Moody’s and Standard & Poor use financial statements as the basis of their ratings analysis •Our revenue bonds have a debt service coverage ratio requirement: •E&G DSC requirement is 1.0 times •Aux DSC requirement is 1.2 times •Failure to achieve these ratios is not an event of default •But it does prevent us from issuing additional revenue bonds until the ratio is achieved again

President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Initial Review of the FY 2026 - FY 2030 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: Each year, as the General Assembly is considering the enactment of the budget for the upcoming fiscal year (FY25), we also begin the budget request cycle for the following year (FY26).
The first budget submittal i n the cycle, in July each year, is the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) which is a rolling five -year plan of proposed University capital projects of $1 million or more funded with unrestricted funds together with related requests for State funding.
The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees has two opportunities to review the proposed CIP, first at the April Board meeting as an item for review and discussion, and next at the June Board meeting for final approval and submission to the State Office o f Management and Budget (OMB).

This submittal is a discussion with the Board in preparation for review and approval at the June Board of Trustees meeting.
Points to Consider: The enclosed presentation provides updates to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including the Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 projects, the Fine Arts Center, the Athletics Complex Renewal, the Biomedical Sciences Building, and New Undergra duate Housing.
It also provides updated cost information for the Memorial Union and Health and Counseling Center projects which have been on hold for the last several years to prioritize housing.
The presentation also highlights several proposed additions to the CIP, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings.
These additions include improving campus accessibility, access control, and building envelope integrity, and refurbishment of the Carothers Library HVAC systems and the university’s water tower.
Additional new projects include the replacement of graduate housing and moving URI’s automotive shop to accommodate undergraduate housing expansion.

Finally, the CIP includes a new project to address destabilization of the access road to the newly completed NBC pier due to significant recent storm damage.
The presentation also notes that given URI’s plans to undertake a Campus Master Plan this year, we do not intend to identify a 2026 GO Bond project in this year’s CIP.
We do intend to submit a GO Bond project in next year’s CIP, when it will be required for consideration by the General Assembly.
